rubrics.evidence: The executive recommendation allocates “50–60%” to customer discovery and experiments and says “do not begin with another broad degree.” Phases 1–3 require discovery conversations, demand/payment tests, and narrow solution pilots.
rubrics.reason: Practical venture-building is the roadmap’s primary activity, while degrees are deferred and subject to explicit incremental-value tests.

rubrics.evidence: Phase 0 defines maintenance weeks of 2–3 hours, standard weeks of 5–7 hours, and optional sprint weeks of 8–12 hours, with protected family time. Founder Institute is conditional on a four-week rehearsal of its 20-hour weekly workload.
rubrics.reason: Work and family compatibility materially determines the recommended formats, operating schedule, and eligibility for more disruptive programs.

rubrics.evidence: Months 1–3 require “18–24 discovery conversations” alongside one lightweight course. The Month 3 gate requires “A cheap next experiment,” followed in Months 4–6 by problem, demand, and payment tests with advance/refine/stop decisions.
rubrics.reason: Market contact starts during initial learning rather than after extensive preparation, and increasingly strong validation gates control subsequent spending and venture development.

rubrics.evidence: Phase 2 applies an assumptions map to users, buyers, channels, pricing, feasibility, and regulation, using Strategyzer’s cost/time/evidence framework. Section 6 requires an interview log, assumption register, experiment ledger, and decision journal within six-week testing cycles.
rubrics.reason: Concrete frameworks and collected market evidence are operationalized into real business decisions. Although in-depth case study work is less developed, the selected resources and learning system clearly prioritize applied evidence over abstract theory.

rubrics.evidence: The HEC comparison weighs €22,950–€24,950 tuition and approximately 20 hours per week against duplicated MBA content and displaced customer work. The selection scorecard includes total cost and displaced venture time, with a veto when a program “relies primarily on prestige or generic content to justify the price.”
rubrics.reason: Cost, workload, and practical return directly shape selection: free foundational resources and experiments lead, while degrees, executive modules, and equity accelerators require demonstrated incremental value.
